title: IA-MNS Corporate Agent
heading: Product and current capabilities
text:
Product and current capabilities
IA-MNS is MNS's corporate AI agent. Its product identity and conversational experience are independent of its first business capability. It can greet users, respond to thanks/wellbeing/identity questions, explain current capabilities and route requests. The only implemented business capability is sales consultation in MNS (Sankhya) and Pilar da Terra (VR Master), chosen with the interface's source selector: net value, quantity and weight (Sankhya only); period/product breakdowns and bounded comparisons ([sources](sales-chat.md#sources)). Purchases, catalog-only product lookup, stock, production, orders, automation and external writes are unavailable. Planned capabilities never appear as available in the catalog.
Social and capability replies are application-authored Portuguese prose selected by a validated bounded intent. OpenAI does not author business numbers, suggest unregistered tools, answer company questions from general knowledge or compose unsupported factual claims. This deliberately limits arbitrary general conversation while allowing a natural social opening without requiring sales details. The UI welcome describes the agent; examples come from registered capabilities. Operational details live in documentation/errors rather than the ordinary conversation shell.

title: IA-MNS Corporate Agent
heading: Implemented architecture
text:
Implemented architecture
`apps/api/src/features/agent/` owns conversations, routing, persistence, progress and HTTP operations. `features/sales/` retains business semantics, strict interpretation, deterministic results, the source orchestration and one adapter per source (Oracle for Sankhya, PostgreSQL for VRMaster). `apps/api/src/modules.ts` injects configured capability executors into the agent; shared runtime files remain module-independent. The agent and legacy sales transport share one owned sales executor and its source pools. The agent references the sales result contract for its current renderable output, while sales implements the agent's execution interface. This intentional boundary does not grant either module mutation authority over the other's tables.
A capability descriptor has a stable id, localized title/description/examples, required permission, executor and resource cleanup. Only configured implementations enter the catalog. General routing instructions serialize the catalog automatically. To add a future capability, implement its owned bounded tools/context/authorization/tests, provide an executor/descriptor, register it at composition, and extend the public versioned result contract and web renderer if necessary. No general prompt rewrite is required. New domains/actions still need actual product authorization and their own safety/idempotency decisions; a registry entry alone cannot implement them.
The route classifier emits a registered capability id or an allowlisted social/unavailable intent. It emits no user-visible prose. It sees the application's earlier replies and which capability awaits an answer; a message it marks unavailable while a permitted capability awaits an answer is offered to that capability, whose own boundary rejects unsupported requests. A sales request then uses the sales interpreter and its deterministic conversation state machine ([AI interpretation](../architecture/ai-interpretation.md)). `runAgentTurn` performs this orchestration independently of persistence, so evaluation runs the same code. User input/history are untrusted data; fixed application policy and schemas govern execution. Mixed supported/unsupported requests are not partially answered. The capability permission is checked before execution, and reading stored business answers checks current capability permission as well as ownership.

title: IA-MNS Corporate Agent
heading: Persistent conversations and context
text:
Persistent conversations and context
PostgreSQL/Prisma owns `agent_conversations` and `agent_turns`; [generated schema](../generated/database/schema.md) records fields, constraints and classification. Conversations have verified owner identity, a bounded editable title (initially derived from the first message), favorite/archive flags, ordering and versioned per-capability context. Turns contain one question, the sales source selected in the interface when it was sent (`sankhya`, `vrmaster` or `all`; earlier turns are `sankhya`, the only source then), client acceptance UUID, ordered sequence, lifecycle state, bounded progress events and a versioned reply snapshot. Reply version 2 holds sales results as one section per queried source; version 1 replies (one Sankhya result) are upgraded when read. No infrastructure credential is stored in these tables.
One turn is accepted at a time under a row lock, without holding a transaction across OpenAI/Oracle work. Acceptance saves the question before starting bounded process-local execution. Replaying the same request UUID, message and source returns the existing turn; a different message or source conflicts. The capability receives the turn's source; the router does not use it. No chargeable provider request is automatically retried. A 120-second database-clock lease handles crashes: stale work becomes interrupted when read or reclaimed, without automatic execution. The process deadline is 90 seconds. Shutdown aborts work and awaits cleanup. This is not a durable workflow engine or an authorization model for future external writes.
Routing uses at most 12 recent completed exchanges: user questions and the application's own replies, with business answers reduced to an "answer delivered" marker, plus the agent context (version 2) naming the capability that awaits an answer. Each capability owns its context version. Sales context version 2 holds structured conversation state: the last executed plan and query, an unanswered request with what it already knows and awaits, and the last 12 sales exchanges, independently of intervening social turns; version 1 contexts upgrade on read. Failed/interrupted turns cannot replace trusted context. Relative periods in a new question use current Sao Paulo time; a follow-up preserves stored explicit filters unless changed. Stored result snapshots are historical answers, not a claim that the ERP remains unchanged. Financial result rows and response prose are never fed back to OpenAI; only questions, application-authored clarification and unavailable messages, filter-only analysis descriptions and structured state are sent. Social turns do not erase sales context or an unanswered sales request.
The generated SDK supports creation, owner-scoped keyset history pages (30), detail pages (40 turns), acceptance, explicit metadata assignment, search and deletion. Active, pinned and archived views belong to the URL via `view`; pinned conversations come first, then modification time and id. Cursor boundaries include the same ordering and filter, preventing cross-filter reuse. Manual titles survive the first turn and are never routing instructions. Rename, pin/unpin, archive/restore and deletion use ownership checks and the same row lock; active execution blocks metadata changes. Archiving preserves messages, answers, favorite state and capability context, and rejects new turns until restored. An already accepted turn can still be replayed while archived. Search uses a bounded, case-insensitive literal substring over owned titles and sent questions, including archives; it does not call OpenAI or search financial result payloads. Search terms and filter-bound cursors use a POST body, not URLs. Search is not accent-insensitive or a semantic/full-text index. The selected conversation id belongs to `/chat/:conversationId`; reloading or opening a previous conversation retrieves PostgreSQL history. Older messages/conversations load in bounded pages. New conversation opens a blank workspace and preserves existing history. Explicit deletion confirms the user's choice and hard-deletes the conversation, context and turns via cascade; active execution blocks deletion.
No prior temporary transcript is migrated: the old UI/process memory had no durable source. Legacy `/sales/chat` endpoints retain their existing temporary semantics for compatibility; the product uses only `/agent` operations. The original numerical/provider tests continue to protect sales behavior.

title: IA-MNS Corporate Agent
heading: Progress and presentation
text:
Progress and presentation
Progress records are emitted immediately before actual operations: understanding the message (routing), preparing a sales query (sales interpretation), consulting sales (the controlled Oracle operation), and organizing results (validated aggregation). A clarification/social/unavailable reply never claims an Oracle phase. Product identification is part of the Oracle query, so there is no fictional separate product-search step. The browser polls persisted progress about once per second while a turn is running; completed/failed history remains recoverable after reload. The latest real stage is displayed with completed stages beneath it. There are no simulated timers or artificial delays.
The Portuguese agent workspace fills the window without the documentation header, outer page margins or a surrounding card. A compact header owns only the agent identity and mobile drawer control. The sidebar owns new conversation, search, pinned/archived views, documentation, theme selection and each conversation's menu (rename, pin/unpin, archive/restore, delete). Desktop history animates between its adjustable column and a 60-pixel icon rail. Drag the right edge or focus its separator and use arrow keys/Home/End to resize between 240 and 420 pixels, additionally limited to 45% of the window; double-click resets to 260 pixels. Expansion and width remain in the in-memory agent session across conversation navigation. On compact screens, history opens in a native modal drawer with focus containment, Escape/backdrop dismissal and focus restoration. Opening history does not resize the underlying chat. The thread and sidebar history scroll independently; the composer stays visible at the bottom and grows with input up to a bounded height. Message/result and composer columns can use up to 1120 pixels, keeping notebook space useful and wide screens readable.
A native `Fonte` selector sits directly above the message box with `MNS (Sankhya)`, `Pilar da Terra (VR Master)` and `Tudo`. It starts at `MNS (Sankhya)`, keeps the choice in the in-memory agent session across conversations, is never written to browser storage, and is disabled only while an unconfirmed submission awaits verification, which replays its own source. Sales turns show the source they were sent with, and a sales answer shows one group per source, headed `Fonte: …`, with its own totals or the reason it has none; `Tudo` answers state that values are not summed.
The workspace keeps sales tables, matched products, decimal/currency formatting, scope, warnings and comparison inspection. Business caveats such as unverified weight units remain beside relevant results. The conversation, results and documentation share the original light/dark semantic palettes from `apps/web/src/styles.css`; the workspace does not override their colors. The initial theme is light, whatever the OS preference; an explicit choice persists only `light`/`dark` under `ia-mns-theme`. Inside PDT Connect the theme follows the PDT's own light/dark choice through the host bridge and the agent offers no theme control there ([identity](identity.md)). Tokens, sidebar state and confidential transcripts remain out of browser storage, logs and URLs. Token changes and workspace unmount clear owned query caches. Reduced-motion preferences disable sidebar/drawer transitions, progress pulsing and smooth scrolling.

title: IA-MNS Corporate Agent
heading: Local lifecycle, privacy and limits
text:
Local lifecycle, privacy and limits
All questions, titles, context and results are CONFIDENTIAL; credentials are RESTRICTED. Local history persists in the named Docker volume until the owner deletes it. Automatic retention, backups/restoration and provider-copy deletion are not implemented. [PH-09](../project/human-actions.md#ph-09) requires a retention/backup/provider policy before shared deployment. Deletion clears live application data and browser query caches; it does not promise erasure of provider copies or future backups. API responses use no-store and telemetry contains only safe correlated diagnostics, never question/result bodies or arbitrary exception text. The default AI trace level logs one content-free `ai_turn_traced` event per turn; the optional content level stores confidential interpretation traces in `agent_turn_traces`, deleted with the conversation and refused in production until PH-09 ([AI tracing](../architecture/ai-interpretation.md#ai-tracing-and-observability)).
Normal credential-free local access remains explicit, loopback-only and forbidden in production. The separate [phone test](../setup.md#phone-testing-on-the-local-network) requires an expiring bearer and an owner-selected private interface; it maps to the same local owner and does not establish employee identity. It represents one local developer, not multiple employee accounts. Normal bearer ownership uses Orion's verifier with tokens issued by the [identity module](identity.md): the owner is the Person UUID, the same for local, PDT Connect and Sankhya sign-in and for every surface, and `sales:read` comes from the identity permission policy. Tenancy and shared hosting remain outside this module. The Oracle SELECT-only account and currency/weight confirmation remain [PH-08](../project/human-actions.md#ph-08). The application maintains read-only Oracle transactions regardless; PostgreSQL writes are confined to its own history.

title: IA-MNS Corporate Agent
heading: Verification
text:
Verification
The owning agent tests use migrated PostgreSQL with restricted grants for restart persistence, concurrency, replay/conflict, interrupted leases, favorite paging, literal search, archive/restore context, owned metadata, cascade deletion and safe failures. Provider schema tests reject invented capabilities/prose and incomplete output. Turn-orchestration tests cover pending-request routing and figure-free router transcripts; integration tests cover content traces, their cascade deletion and capture; the curated [evaluation dataset](../architecture/ai-evaluation.md) replays multi-turn behavior in the ordinary gate. Browser journeys cover the generated SDK, truthful progress, historical navigation/reload, result views, unknown acceptance, credentials, desktop/mobile themes and accessibility. Local real-provider and full-gate evidence is recorded in the project plan; synthetic checks are never described as real ERP reconciliation.

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: Model
text:
Model
The `identity` API module (`apps/api/src/features/identity/`) owns who a person is in IA-MNS and what they may do. The web module (`apps/web/src/features/identity/`) owns sign-in, first access, account and administration screens and the embedded host bridge. Host components only frame the web application and supply proofs: the PDT host page belongs to PDT Connect, and the Sankhya Om add-on is [`apps/sankhya-addon`](../../apps/sankhya-addon/README.md).
Concept
Meaning
Person
The single principal. Its UUID is the access-token `orion_principal_id` and the owner of conversations. Disabled or `merged` into another Person, never hard-deleted.
Local account
Optional login and scrypt password, temporary lockout, optional TOTP second factor with ten single-use recovery codes.
External link
A verified `(provider, issuer, subject)`: PDT `identitySubject` under `PDT_IDENTITY_ISSUER`, or Sankhya `CODUSU` under `SANKHYA_IDENTITY_ISSUER`. One account maps to one Person; one account per provider installation per Person. `established_by` is `proof` (the person proved the account) or `directory` (an owner selected the real Sankhya user). The provider-reported e-mail is kept only as a duplicate hint.
Session
Method (`local`, `pdt`, `sankhya`, `bootstrap`, `enrollment`), surface (`direct`, `pdt`, `sankhya`), assurance (`single`, `mfa`), authentication time, idle and absolute expiry.
Role
`owner`: principal administrator, independent of Sankhya and PDT roles.
Grant
An explicit owner grant of a registered catalog permission.
Physical structure, constraints and classification are in the [schema reference](../generated/database/schema.md) (`identity_*` tables). Names and e-mails are never identity keys. A Person may hold any combination of a local account, a Sankhya link and a PDT link; all of them reach the same history, preferences and permissions.

text:
Sign-in methods and surfaces

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: Direct provider flows
text:
Direct provider flows
`POST /identity/providers/{provider}/start` with `mode: "direct"` creates a 5-minute single-use flow (state, nonce, PKCE verifier) and sets a browser-binding cookie: `ia-mns-pdt` with SameSite=Lax (PDT returns by top-level GET) or `ia-mns-sankhya` with SameSite=None (the Om returns by cross-site form post). Over HTTPS both carry `__Host-` and `Secure`.
PDT: the browser goes to the contract `/integrations/authorize`; PDT redirects to `PDT_IDENTITY_REDIRECT_URI` (`GET /identity/pdt/callback`). Sankhya: the browser goes to `SANKHYA_IDENTITY_AUTHORIZE_URL?state&nonce`; the add-on form-posts `assertion` and `state` to `POST /identity/sankhya/callback`.
The API checks the state ticket and the binding cookie, redeems the PDT code server-side (client secret, PKCE, identity lookup, immediate revoke) or verifies the assertion, then redirects to `/`, `/conta?novo=1` (profile created at first access), `/entrar/primeiro-acesso` (first access waiting for confirmation, or a login started from it with `resumeFirstAccess`), `/conta?vinculado=<provider>` (link or link invitation), `/conta?unificar=<provider>` (consolidation offer), `/conta?confirmado=1` (reauthentication) or `/entrar?erro=CODE`. Callback queries are never logged and responses use `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: Embedded handshake (bridge protocol v1)
text:
Embedded handshake (bridge protocol v1)
The frame calls `POST /identity/providers/{provider}/start` with `mode: "embedded"`. It receives a secret `pendingId` (kept in memory instead of a cookie), the configured host origin and, for PDT, `state` and `codeChallenge` (S256), or, for Sankhya, a `nonce`.
The frame posts to `window.parent` with target origin = host origin:
PDT: `{ v: 1, type: "ia-mns:auth-request", requestId, provider: "pdt", state, code_challenge }`
Sankhya: `{ v: 1, type: "ia-mns:auth-request", requestId, provider: "sankhya", nonce }`
The host answers only its own IA-MNS iframe, with target origin = IA-MNS origin:
PDT: `{ v: 1, type: "ia-mns:auth-response", requestId, code, state, iss }`
Sankhya: `{ v: 1, type: "ia-mns:auth-response", requestId, assertion }`
Failure: `{ v: 1, type: "ia-mns:auth-error", requestId, error }` (for example `pdt_login_required`, `no_authenticated_user`).
The frame sends the proof to `POST /identity/providers/{provider}/complete`; the API verifies it and returns an access token (with `provisioned: true` on an automatic first access), a confirmation request, or a public error.
PDT Connect also sets the display theme: it opens the frame with `?theme=light|dark` and sends `{ v: 1, type: "ia-mns:host-theme", theme }` on load and whenever the person changes the PDT theme. Inside PDT the frame follows that theme, hides its own theme control and stores nothing, so the direct-URL preference is unaffected; a theme message is applied only once the handshake has confirmed the PDT origin. The Sankhya Om sends no theme, and the frame keeps its own light default there.
The frame accepts messages only from the configured host origin and its parent window. These checks are defense in depth: an intercepted code is useless without the client secret and PKCE verifier held by the API, and an assertion is bound to the server nonce and accepted once.
A refused or failed handshake shows its message once, with **Tentar novamente**; nothing retries automatically. Ending an embedded session discards cached person data but keeps the public identity status, so it never starts another handshake by itself.

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: PDT host component (outside this repository)
text:
PDT host component (outside this repository)
The PDT Connect repository (not this one) provides the **IA-MNS** screen (route `/ia-mns`, permission `ia-mns:acessar`), which frames `/embed/pdt` with `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"` and implements step 3 for PDT. It reads its fixed configuration from the PDT parameters `IA_MNS_URL`, `IA_MNS_CLIENT_ID` and `IA_MNS_REDIRECT_URI` through `GET /api/ia-mns/host`, which refuses values outside `PDT_IDENTITY_CLIENTS`, and calls the **existing** contract v1 endpoint `POST /api/auth/integrations/authorize` with the signed-in PDT JWT and that `client_id` and `redirect_uri` (never values sent by the frame). It forwards only the `code`, `state` and `iss` of the returned `redirectUrl`, without navigating. An invalid PDT session answers `pdt_login_required`. The PDT guide `guides/integration-identity.md` documents the screen; client registration, parameters and deployment are PDT operations ([PH-12](../project/human-actions.md#ph-12)).
The embedded flow never visits the registered callback; it only binds the code to the client. IA-MNS therefore offers "Entrar com PDT Connect" on its direct URL only when `PDT_IDENTITY_REDIRECT_URI` is on `IA_MNS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, where the direct flow's binding cookie lives; an installation may register a callback elsewhere for embedded use only.

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: First access, duplicates and linking
text:
First access, duplicates and linking
There is no public account creation. People who use Sankhya or PDT Connect need no prior registration; local credentials come only from the bootstrap, owner invitations, or an authenticated Person adding a password as another method.
**Automatic first access.** A verified PDT or Sankhya account that is not linked creates its Person and link atomically (`person.provisioned` audit, `provisioned: true`), named from the provider-reported name. Concurrent first accesses of one account converge on one Person through the link's unique key.
**When it stops instead.** Creation pauses with `provision_required` and a 10-minute single-use ticket (response body when embedded, HttpOnly cookie when direct) when:
`reason: "candidate"`: the account reports an e-mail equal to the one recorded on another provider's link of an active Person that does not already have an account of this provider. `methods` lists that Person's sign-in methods available here. The person either proves the profile (signs in with one of them, then `POST /identity/provision/link` attaches the account) or states it is not theirs (`POST /identity/provision/create` creates a separate Person). The e-mail alone never links anything.
`reason: "signed_in"` (direct only): the browser already holds a session of a Person when the login started. The person attaches the account to that Person or creates a separate one.
`POST /identity/provision/inspect` describes a pending ticket without consuming it.
**Linking later** (`intent: "link"`) requires a current session with recent authentication (policy window, default 10 minutes) and a new proof. If the account already belongs to a Person whose only method is that account (no password, grants or owner role), the result is `merge_available`; confirming with `POST /identity/merge` (same session) consolidates that Person into the current one. Any other existing owner of the account is refused with `IDENTITY_LINK_CONFLICT`; a different account of the same installation with `IDENTITY_PROVIDER_ALREADY_LINKED`.
**Link invitations.** An owner issues a 72-hour single-use invitation for a Person and provider (`/identidade/vincular#<secret>`). The person signs in to that provider (`intent: "invite"`); the proven account is attached to the invited Person. If the account had already created its own Person with nothing else in it, that Person is consolidated into the invited one.
**Consolidation** (by proof or by an owner) runs in one transaction: links move, the local credential and recovery codes move when the target has none (otherwise they are removed), grants are united, the agent module moves conversations through the `transferOwnership` port supplied at composition (refused with `IDENTITY_MERGE_BUSY` while a turn runs), the source's sessions end and it becomes `merged`. Owner roles are never absorbed. Access tokens already issued to the source remain valid for other modules until they expire (10 minutes).
Unlinking requires recent authentication and never removes the last sign-in method. Owners may unlink for others under the same rule. Every link change is audited.
Recent authentication is restored with the local password (+TOTP) (`POST /identity/me/reauthenticate`), a provider proof with `intent: "reauth"` (only for an account already linked to the Person), or a new embedded handshake.

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: Authorization

title: IA-MNS Identity
heading: Principal administrator, bootstrap and recovery
text:
Principal administrator, bootstrap and recovery
`pnpm identity:bootstrap` (server shell, runtime configuration) prints a single-use 30-minute URL `/identidade/inicial#<secret>` when no active owner exists; `--break-glass` issues one even if owners exist. Both are audited. The page creates the owner with a local account and then requires TOTP before administration.
Administration (`/admin`, `/identity/admin/*`) requires the owner role, a TOTP-assured session (unless a non-production policy makes the second factor optional), and recent authentication for changes (policy window, default 30 minutes). The last active owner cannot be removed or disabled, and owners cannot disable their own TOTP.
Owners create Persons with any combination of: a 72-hour single-use local enrollment invitation (`/identidade/convite#enrollment=<secret>`); a Sankhya user selected from the ERP directory; and link invitations for PDT Connect or Sankhya. Associations always point to a real account: Sankhya users are re-read from the directory on the server (missing or expired-access accounts and accounts already linked elsewhere are refused before anything is created), and PDT accounts require the person's proof because PDT exposes no user directory to IA-MNS. The same actions exist for existing Persons, together with a new enrollment invitation and the reset invitation, which removes the local credential and revokes sessions. Invitation secrets travel in URL fragments, which are not sent to servers, and are removed from history on load.
Owners consolidate two Persons of the same individual (`POST /identity/admin/persons/{personId}/merge`) when they cannot be proven together; owners are never the absorbed Person and overlapping providers are refused.
The Sankhya directory (`GET /identity/admin/sankhya-users`) reads the DBA-provided view named in `SANKHYA_DIRECTORY_VIEW` (columns `CODUSU`, `NOMEUSU`, `NOMEUSUCPLT`, `EMAIL`, `DTLIMACESSO`) in a read-only transaction with its own two-connection pool and a 10-second call timeout, returning at most 20 users. It is off while the view is not configured ([PH-08](../project/human-actions.md#ph-08)). It needs only `SANKHYA_IDENTITY_ISSUER`, not the Om session connector, so it is not gated by PH-11.

**Duration and inactivity.** A direct session ends at sign-in + duration, whatever the use, or when no activity is reported for the inactivity period. The browser reports activity (clicks, typing, scrolling, returning to the tab) with each renewal of its 10-minute access token; renewals of an untouched tab keep the token fresh but do not postpone inactivity. Renewals are serialized across tabs, a tab that returns from sleep renews at once, and a renewal presenting the credential replaced in the last 30 seconds is a concurrent renewal that receives a token without a new credential; later reuse revokes the session. When a session ends, the person returns to `/entrar` with "Sua sessão terminou".
**Recent authentication.** Changes to one's own password, links or second factor need a sign-in or confirmation within the account window; administrative changes within the administrative window. Confirmation uses the password and code, a provider proof, or a new embedded handshake.
**Second factor.** It applies to sign-in with an IA-MNS password (PDT Connect and Sankhya sign-ins are protected by those systems). With `everyone` every such account, and with `administrators` every owner, must use it: an account without it gets `mfa_enrollment_required` after the password (also right after setting a password from an enrollment or reset invitation) and sets up the authenticator before any session opens (`POST /identity/login/mfa-enrollment` and `/confirm`), and cannot remove the factor while required. The code is asked at every sign-in, unless the person chose to remember the browser (offered only when `rememberDeviceDays` > 0, never inside a host page, and to owners only while the requirement is `none`, which production never allows). A remembered browser keeps an HttpOnly `ia-mns-device` cookie whose token is stored hashed in `identity_trusted_devices`; it skips the code but yields an ordinary (not second-factor) session. Password changes, removing the factor, an owner reset or **Voltar a pedir o código em todos** in Minha conta forget remembered browsers.
**Changes.** Saving requires an owner session with the second factor (per policy) and recent administrative confirmation; values outside the limits are refused (`IDENTITY_POLICY_INVALID`), `none` in production is refused (`IDENTITY_POLICY_NOT_ALLOWED`), and newly reduced settings require `acknowledgeReducedSecurity` (`IDENTITY_POLICY_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`). Each change is audited (`policy.updated`) with previous and new values and listed on the screen. Open direct sessions are re-derived at once from their sign-in and last activity (shorter values may end them, including the editor's); second-factor rules apply at the next sign-in, while administration always checks the current rule. Other API instances follow within 15 seconds.
**Not configurable.** Production always requires the second factor for administrators; outside a non-production `none` policy, owners never skip the code through a remembered browser; access tokens stay 10 minutes; embedded sessions renew silently every 10 minutes; ticket, flow and invitation lifetimes, lockout, refresh rotation with reuse detection, rate limits and audit are fixed.
